title: PTGui Control Points Tutorial: Automatic Generation, Manual Refinement, and Masking for a 360 Panorama

locations.name: Tunnel (explicit; photographed in a tunnel as stated in transcript)
locations.basis: Transcript line: 'I've taken the photos in a tunnel' (00:03:14–00:03:17)

summary: This PTGui tutorial explains the concept of control points, how automatic point generation works (in spirit similar to SIFT but not using SIFT in PTGui), and why manual refinement is sometimes necessary. The instructor demonstrates building a fresh project for a fully spherical 360° panorama from four tunnel images, showing how PTGui identifies corresponding points, the role of the cropping circle, and how to inspect, add, move, or delete control points. A control-point table is used to diagnose errors, after which the video covers optimization, removing outliers with the Delete Worst Control Points feature, and achieving a seam-free result with a well-calibrated tripod head. The session also introduces UI aids such as magnification, rectangular selection for group edits, masking to guide where points are generated, and generating points only between selected image pairs or within a masked region.

sections.title: Introduction to control points and how they guide image alignment
concepts: need for manual adjustments when geometry is ambiguous
sections.description: The host introduces the concept of control points, their purpose in aligning two images, and notes that while automated methods exist, manual refinement is sometimes required. Includes a high-level nod to SIFT-like principles and explains normal vs line-type control points.

sections.title: Project setup: tunnel panorama and initial data preparation
sections.description: The instructor begins a fresh project using four tunnel images (90° apart) and explains how PTGui reads EXIF data to infer a circular fisheye lens and the cropping circle, which determines usable image regions.

sections.title: Control Points workflow: generation, inspection, editing, masking, and area-based generation
sections.description: The main workflow is demonstrated: generate initial control points between image pairs, inspect with the magnifier, refine positions with arrow keys or drag, use the Control Points Table to diagnose distances and identify bad points, delete outliers, optimize, and compare results in unblended/visible formats. The video introduces masking to exclude areas and area-based generation between specific image pairs.
